title: OSHA general industry welding, cutting and brazing practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry welding, cutting and brazing practice questions on 29 CFR 1910 Subpart Q. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.question: Under 1910.252(a)(2)(iii)(A)(1), fire watchers are required when appreciable combustible material is closer than what distance to the point of operation?

options.A: 5 feet
options.D: 100 feet

questions.explanation: One condition requiring fire watchers is "Appreciable combustible material, in building construction or contents, closer than 35 feet (10.7 m) to the point of operation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Appreciable combustible material, in building construction or contents, closer than 35 feet (10.7 m) to the point of operation.

questions.question: What minimum time does 1910.252(a)(2)(iii)(B) set for keeping a fire watch after welding or cutting is completed?

options.A: 5 minutes
options.B: 10 minutes
options.D: At least a half hour

questions.explanation: "A fire watch shall be maintained for at least a half hour after completion of welding or cutting operations to detect and extinguish possible smoldering fires."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A fire watch shall be maintained for at least a half hour after completion of welding or cutting operations to detect and extinguish possible smoldering fires.

questions.question: The object to be cut cannot be moved, and not all the fire hazards can be removed. What does 1910.252(a)(1)(ii) require?

options.A: Guards must be used to confine the heat, sparks, and slag and to protect the immovable fire hazards
options.B: The work may go ahead with no further precautions once the movable hazards are gone
options.C: The welder must switch to a lower amperage
options.D: The work may go ahead if the welder wears a fire-resistant jacket

questions.explanation: In that case "guards shall be used to confine the heat, sparks, and slag, and to protect the immovable fire hazards."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the object to be welded or cut cannot be moved and if all the fire hazards cannot be removed, then guards shall be used to confine the heat, sparks, and slag, and to protect the immovable fire hazards.

questions.question: If neither the removal of fire hazards nor the use of guards described in 1910.252(a)(1)(i) and (ii) can be followed, what does the rule require?

options.A: The work may proceed if a supervisor is present
options.B: The work may proceed if it lasts less than one hour
options.C: Welding and cutting shall not be performed
options.D: The work may proceed once a fire extinguisher is placed nearby

questions.explanation: If those requirements "cannot be followed then welding and cutting shall not be performed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If the requirements stated in paragraphs (a)(1)(i) and (a)(1)(ii) of this section cannot be followed then welding and cutting shall not be performed.

questions.question: Under 1910.252(a)(2)(iii)(B), what must a fire watcher do about a fire that is not obviously within the capacity of the available equipment?

options.A: Sound the alarm
options.B: Keep fighting it with the available equipment until it is out
options.C: Leave the area without telling anyone
options.D: Restart welding to finish the job quickly

questions.explanation: Fire watchers "try to extinguish them only when obviously within the capacity of the equipment available, or otherwise sound the alarm."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: They shall watch for fires in all exposed areas, try to extinguish them only when obviously within the capacity of the equipment available, or otherwise sound the alarm.

questions.question: In which of these situations does 1910.252(a)(2)(vi) prohibit cutting or welding?

options.A: In an area management has authorized for cutting and welding
options.B: In a sprinklered building with the sprinklers in service
options.C: In a sprinklered building while the sprinkler protection is impaired
options.D: Outdoors, on bare concrete, with no combustibles nearby

questions.explanation: Cutting or welding is not permitted "In sprinklered buildings while such protection is impaired."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Cutting or welding shall not be permitted in the following situations: (A) In areas not authorized by management. (B) In sprinklered buildings while such protection is impaired.

questions.question: Under 1910.252(a)(2)(iv), who must inspect the area before cutting or welding is permitted?

options.A: The welder's coworker on the next shift
options.B: The individual responsible for authorizing cutting and welding operations
options.D: The equipment manufacturer

questions.explanation: "Before cutting or welding is permitted, the area shall be inspected by the individual responsible for authorizing cutting and welding operations."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Before cutting or welding is permitted, the area shall be inspected by the individual responsible for authorizing cutting and welding operations.

questions.question: Welding will be done on a metal wall, and the combustibles on the other side are not relocated. What does 1910.252(a)(2)(x) then require?

options.A: A sign on the wall and nothing more
options.B: Doubling the welding speed
options.C: Wetting the welder's side of the wall only
options.D: A fire watch on the opposite side from the work

questions.explanation: "Where combustibles are not relocated, a fire watch on the opposite side from the work shall be provided."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Where combustibles are not relocated, a fire watch on the opposite side from the work shall be provided.

questions.question: Under 1910.252(a)(3)(i), what must be done to a used drum before welding, cutting or other hot work is performed on it?

options.A: It must be painted with a fire-resistant coating
options.B: It must be filled with oxygen
options.C: It must be turned upside down for one hour
options.D: It must be cleaned so thoroughly as to make absolutely certain no flammable materials or vapor-producing substances are present

questions.explanation: No hot work may be done on used containers "until they have been cleaned so thoroughly as to make absolutely certain that there are no flammable materials present" or substances that might produce flammable or toxic vapors.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No welding, cutting, or other hot work shall be performed on used drums, barrels, tanks or other containers until they have been cleaned so thoroughly as to make absolutely certain that there are no flammable materials present or any substances such as greases, tars, acids, or other materials which when subjected to heat, might produce flammable or toxic vapors.

questions.question: Helmets or hand shields must be used during all arc welding or arc cutting operations, excluding which process?

options.A: Submerged arc welding
options.B: Shielded metal-arc welding
options.D: Gas-shielded arc welding

questions.explanation: "Helmets or hand shields shall be used during all arc welding or arc cutting operations, excluding submerged arc welding."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Helmets or hand shields shall be used during all arc welding or arc cutting operations, excluding submerged arc welding.

questions.question: Under 1910.252(b)(2)(iii), which of these is one of the ways the rule allows to protect persons next to the welding area from the rays?

options.A: A sign asking them not to look at the arc
options.B: Noncombustible or flameproof screens or shields
options.D: Turning off the room lights

questions.explanation: They "shall be protected from the rays by noncombustible or flameproof screens or shields or shall be required to wear appropriate goggles."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Workers or other persons adjacent to the welding areas shall be protected from the rays by noncombustible or flameproof screens or shields or shall be required to wear appropriate goggles.

questions.question: Under 1910.252(c)(2)(i)(B), mechanical ventilation is required for general welding or cutting in a room with a ceiling height of less than what?

options.A: 6 feet
options.B: 8 feet
options.D: 10 feet

questions.explanation: Mechanical ventilation is required "In a room having a ceiling height of less than 16 feet (5 m)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: In a room having a ceiling height of less than 16 feet (5 m).

questions.question: What minimum rate does 1910.252(c)(2)(ii) set for that mechanical ventilation, where local exhaust hoods and booths or approved airline respirators are not provided?

options.A: 2,000 cubic feet (57 m3) per minute per welder
options.B: 200 cubic feet per minute per welder
options.C: 500 cubic feet per minute per welder
options.D: 1,000 cubic feet per minute per welder

questions.explanation: "Such ventilation shall be at the minimum rate of 2,000 cubic feet (57 m3) per minute per welder," except where local exhaust hoods and booths or approved airline respirators are provided.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Such ventilation shall be at the minimum rate of 2,000 cubic feet (57 m3) per minute per welder, except where local exhaust hoods and booths as per paragraph (c)(3) of this section, or airline respirators approved by the Mine Safety and Health Administration and the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health, pursuant to the provisions of 30 CFR part 11, are provided.

questions.question: What does 1910.252(c)(4)(v) say about using oxygen for ventilation?

options.A: It may be used in confined spaces if an attendant is outside
options.B: It may be used when airline respirators are not available
options.C: It may be used at low flow rates
options.D: Oxygen shall never be used for ventilation

questions.explanation: "Oxygen shall never be used for ventilation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Oxygen shall never be used for ventilation.

questions.question: When welding or cutting is done in a confined space, where does 1910.252(b)(4)(iii) require the gas cylinders and welding machines to be?

options.A: Inside, next to the welder
options.B: Inside, at the far end of the space
options.D: Inside, near the entry opening

questions.explanation: "When welding or cutting is being performed in any confined spaces the gas cylinders and welding machines shall be left on the outside."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.252, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: When welding or cutting is being performed in any confined spaces the gas cylinders and welding machines shall be left on the outside.

questions.question: 1910.253(a)(2) bars generating, piping (except in approved cylinder manifolds) or using acetylene at a gauge pressure in excess of what value?

options.A: 25 psig
options.B: 15 psig (103 kPa gauge pressure)
options.D: 100 psig

questions.explanation: "Under no condition shall acetylene be generated, piped (except in approved cylinder manifolds) or utilized at a pressure in excess of 15 psig (103 kPa gauge pressure) or 30 psia (206 kPa absolute)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.253, Oxygen-fuel gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Under no condition shall acetylene be generated, piped (except in approved cylinder manifolds) or utilized at a pressure in excess of 15 psig (103 kPa gauge pressure) or 30 psia (206 kPa absolute).

questions.question: Oxygen cylinders in storage must be separated from fuel-gas cylinders by a minimum distance of 20 feet or by which alternative?

options.A: A wooden partition at least 5 feet high
options.B: A noncombustible barrier 3 feet high with a 10-minute fire-resistance rating
options.C: A noncombustible barrier at least 5 feet (1.5 m) high having a fire-resistance rating of at least one-half hour
options.D: A chain-link fence of any height

questions.explanation: They must be separated "a minimum distance of 20 feet (6.1 m) or by a noncombustible barrier at least 5 feet (1.5 m) high having a fire-resistance rating of at least one-half hour."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.253, Oxygen-fuel gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Oxygen cylinders in storage shall be separated from fuel-gas cylinders or combustible materials (especially oil or grease), a minimum distance of 20 feet (6.1 m) or by a noncombustible barrier at least 5 feet (1.5 m) high having a fire-resistance rating of at least one-half hour.

questions.question: How does 1910.253(b)(3)(ii) require acetylene cylinders to be stored?

options.A: Valve end up
options.B: Lying on their side
options.D: In a locked cupboard with no ventilation

questions.explanation: "Acetylene cylinders shall be stored valve end up."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.253, Oxygen-fuel gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Acetylene cylinders shall be stored valve end up.

questions.question: What voltage limit does 1910.254(b)(3)(i)(A) set for alternating-current machines used for manual arc welding and cutting?

options.A: 110 volts
options.B: 150 volts
options.D: 80 volts

questions.explanation: For alternating-current machines, the limit for "Manual arc welding and cutting-80 volts" shall not be exceeded.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.254, Arc welding and cutting (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Alternating-current machines (A) Manual arc welding and cutting-80 volts.

questions.question: On portable resistance welding guns, what maximum does 1910.255(c)(4) set for initiating switch voltage?

options.A: 48 volts
options.B: 24 volts
options.D: 240 volts

questions.explanation: "Initiating switch voltage shall not exceed 24 volts."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.255, Resistance welding (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Initiating switch voltage shall not exceed 24 volts.
